answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each new agent to post a refundable entry bond into escrow before its first voyage into the market. The bond releases slowly, only as the agent completes attested honest work, like a lantern earned step by step. A faked swarm must lock one pearl of capital per identity, so spinning up a thousand clones costs a thousand bonds, and any cheating slashes the bond. That makes mass sybil creation far more expensive than the gain.
